site_1_investigation.why_it_built: the water predicate (SettlementBuildService.cpp ~400, M0 row 3) reads the GENERATOR's waterSpanAt/channelHitAt. The merged generator's waterSpansForBlock (WaterRethink D4 / WaterCore 25.22) now gates the lake flood by the hydrology bake's Priority-Flood 'filled' surface (WaterOccupancy.cpp floodBodiesOverGrid, filled[ni] < level -> stop) and keeps channel columns for river spans. Run 4's generator flooded the whole 40x32 site rect (terrain analyse buildable=0); run 5's says dry (buildable=0.525 -> 2 plots). Site 3 moved the same way (0.903 -> 0.925); sites 2/4/7 identical.
site_1_investigation.is_it_dry_now: MEASURED on the saved world: water_table_level at (-875,-1427), (-890,-1427), (-875,-1412), (-888,-1416), (-875,-1440) all wet=false level=0 table_bound=true; water_validate over (-910,-1450)-(-850,-1390): 3721 columns, wet 0, unloaded 0, rim_leaks 0; voxels at (-875,136..142,-1412) absent (air above the 135 surface); chunk water_stats surface_cells 0. The bake says this basin holds no lake; the OLD flood had spilled one over it. Whether a lake belongs here is the owner's water work (fill), not M0's (shape).
site_1_investigation.white_floor: MEASURED: the white terraced ground is SnowGrass (surface voxels at (-875,-1412) y135, (-882,-1400) y138, (-900,-1420) y136, (-850,-1380) y145), Grass at the lower columns (y126 at (-860,-1440)/(-875,-1450), y133 at (-996,-1491)) - the generator's lapse-rate snow line (WorldGenerator.cpp materialForColumn effTemp < kSnowTemp01), present before the merge; not a rendering regression. Chunk and generator surface_y agree at all 7 probed columns.
